lesson.summary: Security on AWS is shared. AWS is responsible for security of the cloud, which covers the hardware, software, networking and facilities that run its services. The customer is responsible for security in the cloud, which covers their own data, who can access it, and how they configure the services they use. The split moves with the service: on EC2 you patch the operating system yourself, while more managed services shift that work to AWS.
keyPoints: AWS handles security of the cloud: hardware, software, networking and the physical facilities of its data centers
Customers handle security in the cloud: their data, who can access it, and how their services are configured
Customers choose and manage encryption of their own data, including client-side encryption before upload
On Amazon EC2 the customer patches the guest operating system and any applications installed on the instance
AWS patches the underlying infrastructure that runs the services
The responsibility split changes with the service; managed and abstracted services move more of the work to AWS
lesson.simpleSummary: AWS looks after the building and the hardware. You look after what you put inside it: your data, who can open it, and the software you run.
lesson.mnemonic: Naruto hint: AWS guards the Hidden Leaf village walls. You guard your own house and the scrolls inside it.

scenarios.text: A startup runs its web application on Amazon EC2 instances. The team wants to know who is responsible for installing security updates to the operating system on those instances.

questions.prompt: Which task is AWS responsible for under the shared responsibility model?

options.text: Patching the guest operating system on an EC2 instance
Physical security of the data centers that host AWS services
Deciding which employees can access the company's data
Encrypting customer data on the customer's side before upload

questions.explanation: AWS is responsible for security of the cloud, which includes the physical facilities of its data centers. Patching the guest operating system, deciding who can access data, and client-side encryption are customer tasks.
questions.simplePrompt: Which task does AWS take care of?
questions.simpleExplanation: AWS protects the buildings and the physical data centers that run its services.

questions.prompt: Which TWO tasks are the customer's responsibility? (Choose two.)

options.text: Physical security of the data centers
Managing who can access the data they store
Encrypting data on the client side before it is uploaded
Replacing failed hardware inside AWS data centers
Keeping the underlying infrastructure hypervisor patched

questions.explanation: Access management and client-side encryption are configured by the customer, which makes them security in the cloud. Data center hardware, physical security and the infrastructure that runs the services are AWS's responsibility.
questions.simplePrompt: Which two tasks are yours to look after?
questions.simpleExplanation: Your job is to manage who can open your data and to protect the traffic and data you control.

questions.prompt: Who is responsible for installing security updates to the operating system on the EC2 instances in this scenario?

options.text: AWS, because it owns the hardware
The customer, because the customer manages the guest operating system
The operating system vendor, with neither AWS nor the customer involved
AWS and the customer must each install the same update

questions.explanation: On EC2 the customer patches the guest operating system and the software installed on it. AWS patches the infrastructure under the services. Owning the hardware does not make AWS responsible for the guest OS.
questions.simplePrompt: A startup runs its website on EC2 servers. Who keeps the operating system up to date?
questions.simpleExplanation: You do. On EC2 you update the operating system and the software you install. AWS updates the hardware under it.

questions.statement: On Amazon EC2, AWS patches the guest operating system on your instance for you.
questions.explanation: False. On EC2 you patch the guest operating system and the applications you install. AWS patches the underlying infrastructure.
questions.simplePrompt: True or false: on EC2, AWS updates the operating system for you.
questions.simpleExplanation: False. On EC2 you update the operating system. AWS keeps the hardware under it safe.

questions.prompt: Match each task with the side of the shared responsibility model that owns it.

pairs.left: Physical security of the data center
Patching the guest operating system on EC2
Deciding who can access stored data

questions.explanation: Facilities, hardware and global infrastructure belong to security of the cloud, which AWS owns. Guest OS patching and access decisions are configured by the customer, so they are security in the cloud.
questions.simplePrompt: Match each task to who is responsible for it.
questions.simpleExplanation: Buildings and hardware belong to AWS. Updating the operating system and choosing who can open your data belong to you.

questions.prompt: Type the phrase for the part of security that AWS owns, in the form security ... the cloud.
questions.explanation: Security of the cloud is the part AWS owns: the hardware, software, networking and facilities that run its services. Security in the cloud is the customer's part.
questions.simplePrompt: Type the phrase in the form security ... the cloud, for the part of security that AWS owns.
questions.simpleExplanation: It is security of the cloud. AWS guards the physical and underlying parts of its services.
